summary:
TerraClue is an educational web application that helps high school and college students investigate how Earth is changing where they live. Users select a Brazilian city and an environmental variable - average temperature, precipitation, or solar radiation - and the application retrieves monthly NASA POWER data from 2001 to 2025.

TerraClue visualizes the resulting time series, removes the regular seasonal cycle, estimates the rate of change per decade through linear regression, and uses a 95% confidence interval to determine whether the trend is statistically significant. An unsupervised Isolation Forest model also highlights unusual months for further investigation.

The project addresses the challenge by showing what is changing, where it is changing, how quickly it is changing, and whether the measured trend is significant. Its accessible explanations introduce students to trends, statistical confidence, and machine-learning anomalies without requiring advanced climate science knowledge. TerraClue makes NASA Earth science data easier to explore while clearly communicating uncertainty and scientific limitations.
details:
TerraClue is an educational web application that allows users to investigate environmental trends near four Brazilian cities: Florianópolis, Manaus, Brasília, and São Paulo. Users select a location and one of three variables - average air temperature, precipitation, or surface solar radiation. The application then retrieves monthly NASA POWER data from 2001 to 2025.

To make long-term change easier to identify, TerraClue removes the regular seasonal cycle by comparing observations with the long-term average for each calendar month. It applies linear regression to estimate the rate of change per decade and calculates a 95% confidence interval to indicate whether the trend is statistically significant. An unsupervised Isolation Forest model analyzes trend residuals and month-to-month changes, highlighting the 5% most unusual observations for further investigation.

The intended audience is high school and college students, educators, and members of the public with an interest in Earth science. TerraClue explains trends, statistical significance, and anomalies in accessible language. Its main benefit is transforming analysis-ready NASA data into evidence that students can explore without requiring advanced climate science or programming knowledge.

The project was developed as a browser-based application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It connects directly to the NASA POWER Monthly API and uses data derived from MERRA-2 for temperature and corrected precipitation, and CERES-associated products for solar radiation. Git was used for version control, and Netlify hosts the public application. No hardware, database, backend server, or synthetic scientific data is required.

TerraClue is creative because it combines statistical trend analysis, interpretable machine learning, interactive visualization, and science education in a lightweight application that runs entirely in the browser. The project prioritizes transparency: it distinguishes an unusual observation from a dangerous event, reports inconclusive trends honestly, and explains how each result was calculated.

Important considerations include seasonal variability, missing or invalid observations, NASA POWER grid-cell resolution, statistical uncertainty, and accessibility for non-specialists. TerraClue describes historical patterns rather than forecasting future climate, and its results do not replace expert-reviewed climatological studies.
